name: What are the most common mistakes in bathroom additions?

mainEntity.name: What problems cause bathroom additions to run over budget or fail inspection?
mainEntity.text: What problems cause bathroom additions to run over budget or fail inspection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom additions fail most often when the design looks good but does not account for construction reality. Common mistakes include placing fixtures too close together, ignoring the drain slope, forgetting ventilation, and assuming the room can be built without permits. Another major issue is underestimating hidden conditions such as slab cutting, outdated wiring, or framing repairs. Homeowners also get into trouble when they choose finishes before confirming the actual layout, because even small changes can force plumbing or framing revisions. A better approach is to confirm the wet wall, fixture locations, and permit path first, then finalize tile and finish selections. That sequence reduces change orders and keeps the project moving. For an addition, the best defense against mistakes is early planning and a contractor who can explain the technical constraints before demolition starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common mistakes are poor fixture spacing, ignoring plumbing access, underestimating ventilation needs, and skipping permit review. Choosing finishes before the layout is solved can also cause expensive changes. Hidden structural or slab conditions are another common source of delays and cost overruns.
